name: Haircut for face shape

image.caption: How to choose a haircut and hairstyle to your face shape

lead: This is the habit of choosing a haircut based on whether your face is oval, round, square and so on. Stylists and looksmaxxing advocates say particular cuts can balance or flatter particular proportions, so the overall look comes across as more harmonious.

Practitioners say hair length and volume can make a face appear more balanced. A general hairstyle reference notes that a style's look depends on factors including face and head shape, hair type and growth patterns. No published studies testing face-shape matching rules were found.

paras: People identify their face shape from a mirror, photos or a stylist's assessment, then bring reference cuts to a barber or stylist who adjusts length, volume and fringe to suit. It is a one-time choice that is refreshed with each cut, and the result is visible right away.
The practice carries no reported medical risks. A cut you dislike grows out over weeks, and hair type and growth patterns also affect how any style turns out.

angle.text: Matching a haircut to your face shape is meant to balance your proportions so you look more flattering overall. Stylists use it as a rule of thumb, and no published studies have tested the rules.

lead: Choosing a haircut for face shape means picking a style that suits the proportions of the face, usually by sorting faces into categories such as oval, round, square, heart or diamond. Stylists and looksmaxxing communities say the right cut can balance the face: adding height or volume where it is narrow, or reducing width where it is broad, so the overall silhouette looks more harmonious.

A general hairstyle reference lists face and head shape, viewed from different angles, among the physical factors that shape a style's appearance, alongside natural hair type, growth patterns, body proportions, the stylist's judgment and the wearer's desired self-image [1]. Facial shape itself is determined mainly by the bones of the face plus soft tissue and is considered a factor in perceived attractiveness.
The hairstyle article does not give face-shape-to-haircut rules, and no published study has tested face-shape matching rules.
infobox: Oval, round, square, heart, diamond, oblong

paras: The idea is that hair can add or reduce visual width, length or angularity so the overall silhouette appears balanced. Stylists commonly sort faces into categories to apply it. The hairstyle article cites face and head shape as one factor alongside natural hair type, growth patterns and the stylist's judgment [1].

Hairstyles are also described as signals of identity, age and social standing, and natural, healthy-looking hair is linked to perceived health, which the same reference suggests helps explain hair's role in attraction [1].

Facial shape is determined mainly by the maxilla, mandible, nasal, zygomatic and frontal bones plus soft tissue, and is considered a factor in perceived attractiveness. That reference contains no research linking face-shape categories to hairstyle selection.

Haircut advice features in looksmaxxing and bodybuilding forums as a cheap upgrade. On T Nation, users posted photos in threads asking for haircut input, and discussed how brow shaping and cut interact [2].
